Local Community Initiatives 
 
Community Response to Emergency Events 
 
The Community Directorate is working across all directorates to 
ensure Tipperary County Council has a coordinated response to 
severe weather events. The Community Response Subgroup 
continues to meet regularly, with the latest meeting held online on 
13th May, where members were updated on progress relating to 
the 32 Community Support Centres (CSCs) identified across the 
county. In addition, four transportable generators funded by the 
Department of Rural and Community Development & the 
Gaeltacht have arrived and will support CSCs during power 
outages once the necessary changeover switch installations are 
completed. The subgroup will meet again on 24th June to review 
further progress and establish a Humanitarian Sub-group to 
support the CSC network. 
 
Local Community Development Committee (LCDC)  
 
A national campaign led by the Department of Rural and 
Communtiy Development and the Gaeltacht, in partnership with 
Local Government Ireland was launched on 1st May. The campaign 
is titled “Our LCDCs – Building better communities together – le 
chéile” and is accompanied by a new national website 
www.gov.ie/lcdc . 
 
Cllr. Declan Burgess, Project Coordinator, Comhairle na nÓg 
delivered a presentation about Tipperary Comhairle na nÓg to the 
members at the April LCDC meeting.

Social Inclusion Community Activation Programme 
(SICAP) 
The LCDC have agreed Annual Plans for SICAP with NTDC and 
STDC for 2026.  
KPIs have been set across the SICAP Goals. 
 
Goal 1: To contribute to building more sustainable inclusive and 
empowered communities. NTDC plan to work with 40 community 
groups during the year and STDC with 37 groups. 
 
Goal 2: This goal aims to empower disadvantaged people to 
improve the quality of their lives. Both development companies 
have targets to work with 485 individuals on a one-to one basis 
during the year.  
 
A Mid-year review process will commence in late June. 
 
Rural Community Public Lighting Grant 
A new Rural Community Public Lighting Grant has been 
launched by Tipperary County Council, inviting applications 
from community groups and sports clubs for small-scale 
lighting projects. Funding of up to €5,000 per project is 
available, subject to criteria including connection to an existing 
electricity supply and ongoing maintenance by the applicant 
group.  
The initiative aims to support improved safety and accessibility 
in rural areas through appropriate, energy-efficient lighting 
schemes. Applications are currently open, with a closing date of 
22 June 2026.

Expressions of Interest for the Building and Land Acquisition 
Grant under the Town & Village Renewal Scheme have been 
assessed. Work is now underway with shortlisted applicants to

CLÁR Grant Programme 
The strong level of interest in the CLÁR Programme highlights

support. The expressions of interests received have been

Age Friendly 
The Annual Age Friendly EXPO and Showcase will take place on 
Thursday 18th June 2026 at the TUS Campus, Thurles. The 
event will promote positive ageing in County Tipperary through 
information stands, services, supports and talks aimed at 
helping older people remain active, informed and connected

Power of People and Place  
Work on the Community Facility Audit under the Local 
Economic and Community Plan (LECP) “Power of People and 
Place” action is progressing well and has now entered its final 
phase, with surveys underway in the remaining Municipal 
Districts of Nenagh and Clonmel. The audit aims to develop a 
comprehensive picture of community facilities across the 
county to support future planning, investment and community 
development initiatives. 
The next stage of the project will focus on finalising and 
validating the data gathered and developing a practical, user-
friendly web-based resource to improve access to information 
on community facilities across County Tipperary.

Healthy Ireland 
 
Service Level Agreements have been finalised with Silver Arch 
FRC, NTDC and the Tipperary Holistic Health Network to deliver 
programmes in North Tipperary focused on social inclusion, 
older adults and health promotion. Funding of €19,562 has 
been secured under the 2026 Play and Recreation Capital Fund 
for improvement works at Dromineer Playground. In addition, 
Healthy Tipperary secured €51,000 under the Creative Ireland 
Health and Wellbeing in the Community Fund for a regional 
CAMHS project, and a further €16,000 under the Period Dignity 
/ Period Poverty Fund to support local needs. The new Healthy 
Ireland Portal will also support future community wellbeing 
planning and GIS mapping in Tipperary. 
A Step2theBeat training workshop was delivered to staff 
working across Day Care Centres, Older Adult Services and 
Disability Services throughout the county. The training 
equipped staff with new skills and activities to help encourage 
greater movement and physical activity among service users. 
The workshop was delivered in response to strong demand 
following the success of the 2025 training programme.

Tipperary LocalCommunity Safety Partnership 
 
Tipperary Local Community Safety Partnership (LCSP) has 
commenced community consultations and safety surveys to 
support the preparation of a new three-year Community Safety 
Plan for County Tipperary. The plan will provide a coordinated 
and evidence-based framework to enhance community safety 
and wellbeing, informed by national and local priorities as well 
as the lived experiences of communities across the county.

community and youth groups through workshops and surveys, 
while also visiting libraries countywide to support members of 
the public in completing the survey and sharing their views and 
concerns. The public survey remains open on the Tipperary 
County Council website until the end of August, with further 
public and stakeholder consultation events to be announced in 
the coming months. 
 
LCSP and Tipperary PPNs Community safety and 
Community resilience Event:  
On Tuesday, 21 April, Tipperary PPN and Tipperary LCSP jointly 
hosted a Community Safety and Resilience Event in 
Upperchurch. The event brought together representatives from 
Tipperary Age Friendly, Healthy Homes, Tipperary Fire Service, 
Muintir na Tíre and Crime Prevention Officer Sgt. John 
McCormack to discuss a range of topics including home and 
vehicle safety, CCTV, data protection, healthy homes supports, 
community safety surveys and severe weather preparedness. 
Further Community Safety Days are planned across the county, 
and community groups interested in hosting an event are 
encouraged to contact Tipperary LCSP for support and 
information.

TOURISM 
 
 
Tourism and Outdoor Recreation 
The Caravan and Camping Feasibility Study has completed 
consultation across all Municipal Districts and has now 
progressed to Phase 2, focusing on identifying viable 
opportunities and delivery options. Under the ORIS 5 Signature 
Sites Beyond Accessibility Action Plan, detailed accessibility 
audits have been completed at key locations including Littleton 
Labyrinth/Lough Derg Bhile, Cahir Castle to Swiss Cottage, the 
Suir Blueway, Ballina Amenity Park and Fethard Town Park. 
The next phase will include engagement with the Tipperary 
Disability Group and stakeholder surveys to help ensure the 
final recommendations reflect lived experience and accessibility 
best practice. 
The Suir Blueway Tipperary Cluster Development Programme 
hosted a recruitment webinar on 12 May to encourage 
additional tourism providers to join the initiative across Cahir, 
Carrick-on-Suir and Clonmel. Membership has now reached 45 
businesses, with a target of 60. 
Tipperary Tourism continued a strong programme of promotion 
and capacity-building throughout May. Following Tipperary’s 
inclusion in Lonely Planet’s top destinations for 2026, a 
campaign featuring Roz Purcell generated significant national 
exposure, including coverage on RTÉ Lifestyle with a reach of 
over one million people. Travel content creator Chris Connolly 
(Explore with Criostoir) also visited the county to showcase 
Tipperary’s food, heritage and outdoor experiences to an 
audience of more than 200,000.

Community Climate Action Programme

Minister on the successful projects was made on 21st May with the good 
news that 30 projects across the county have been approved for funding, 
and that we received an extra allocation of €106k bringing the total for 
Tipperary to €806k.    The funding will enable community and voluntary 
groups to carry out important projects such as solar installations, building

Voids Overview  
 
 
 
Total number of voids per district 
 
In accordance with Circular 08/2026, the department is looking for local 
authorities to put in place adequate structures to ensure the effective and 
efficient management of the local authority housing stock and to transition 
from a largely response based approach to housing stock maintenance, to 
a strategic and informed planned maintenance approach, informed by stock 
condition surveys. The new planned maintenance approach sets out to 
improve the overall condition of housing stock with annual programmes of 
works in each district that will target the houses in most need of 
investment. 
In tandem with the new planned maintenance approach, turnaround times 
for voids will be required to reduce. The reduction in turnaround times for 
voids will largely be achieved by a reduced scope of works prior to 
reletting. Any other improvement works will be carried out the through a 
planned maintenance approach with tenants in-situ. 
As part of this transition, discussions are ongoing with district staff to 
facilitate the stock condition surveys required and to agree minimum works 
required to relet voids. The previous approach of upgrading void units to a 
BER C1 will now need to be reviewed in light of the turnaround times 
required nationally.   
Normal and ongoing reactive maintenance repairs carried out by the district 
maintenance staff in accordance with the responsibilities set out in the 
tenant’s handbook will remain unchanged.
